# Audit marketing before ship

Audit the supplied package against its actual audience, product truth, channel, and intended action.
Do not turn taste into a deterministic phrase detector.

## Freeze the audit scope

Name the exact artifacts, versions, product evidence, audience, channels, constraints, and claims in
scope. Note missing context. Do not expand into unrelated files, rewrite the strategy, or treat an
unavailable artifact as defective.

## Inspect seven dimensions

1. product truth and unsupported claims;
2. audience and costly-moment specificity;
3. promise, mechanism, proof, and objection logic;
4. comprehension, hierarchy, and argument continuity;
5. voice, read-aloud rhythm, and generic or templated residue;
6. channel and format fit;
7. action clarity, consent, and strength of the CTA.

Check names, numbers, links, dates, quotes, attribution, legal or platform-sensitive claims, and
cross-artifact consistency. Judge phrases in context; no word or cadence is defective merely because
an AI system often uses it.

## Report only actionable findings

Rank each finding as **blocking**, **material**, or **minor**. Include the location, observed text or
behavior, why it matters, supporting evidence, and the smallest safe correction. Keep detection and
fixing separate so the operator can accept, revise, or decline a change.

Identify what survives unchanged. Preserve distinctive, useful, and historically valuable work even
when adjacent units need revision. Never delete, archive, rewrite, or label work useless without
explicit scope and authority.

## Verdict and re-verification

Return:

- audit scope and missing inputs;
- findings by severity;
- what survives;
- proposed corrections;
- **ready for human release review** or **not ready for human release review**;
- recheck list for claims, numbers, links, names, and CTA strength after accepted fixes.

The verdict is evidence for a human decision, not permission to publish, release, delete, or perform
external actions.

Before delivery, load the recovered method instead of paraphrasing it:

- [audit flow](references/audit-flow.md) for detect-only scanning and report shape;
- [noise filter](references/noise-filter.md) before the report writes;
- [report template](references/report-template.md) for the ship artifact;
- [fix routing](references/fix-routing.md) and [polish flow](references/polish-flow.md) when the
  operator asks for proposed fixes;
- [reverify gate](references/reverify-gate.md) after any Accepted fix;
- [quality feedback](references/quality-feedback-protocol.md) when overrides or repeated misses
  appear.

Write durable audit artifacts to `.forsvn/artifacts/mkt/audit-marketing/` when the host has one;
otherwise return them inline. If the host cannot run a multi-step polish loop, use [sequential
fallback](fallbacks/sequential.md). Detect ≠ fix. Available public fixers (`vietnamese`,
`copy`) or an operator-named tool may be routed fixes; none of them — and no critic score —
grants release authority.
